issue.title: Absorb already-captured refs into a new multi-URL collection (--absorb)

task_type_fields.proposal: Add a way (the bob-cli-7v plan calls it `--absorb`) for `bob ref create URL URL…` to fold already-captured single-URL references into a new collection instead of refusing. Today any part already in a PDF-backed ref note or queued intake PDF refuses the whole collection (`N of M URLs are already in the library … remove those references first`, src/native/highlights_ref/collection.rs check_collection_overlap), which preserves the one-URL-one-reference invariant. The motivating case: on 2026-10-11 Bryan captured Stripe's two-part "Minions" series as two references a minute apart and linked them by hand; merging them today means deleting both refs (and losing their annotations, reading tasks, and audio) before re-capturing. The design must decide what happens to the absorbed notes, PDFs, annotations, ^ref tasks, dependency edges, and audio, and how `find`, routing, and `duplicate_identity` see the transition. Proposed by the plan of epic bob-cli-7v (out-of-scope list: "--absorb for existing refs"), recorded by the bob-cli-7v land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-7v deliberately refuses partial overlap to keep one URL in one reference; absorbing existing refs is a migration with its own design space (shared with bob-cli-39's recapture/versioning question) that the epic's plan defers to v2.

issue.creation_reason: Epic bob-cli-7v refuses any collection whose parts are already captured, so a series captured part by part (Stripe Minions) cannot be merged without deleting its refs; the plan deferred --absorb to v2.
